terms.definition: the permanent name of a running brainstem, object or door. Format: `rappid:@<owner>/<slug>:<64-lowercase-hex>`. The tail is minted once from UUIDv4 octets or a public key (SPKI DER), never from the owner/slug name. See [[Identity and the Rappid]].
continuity across changing content. In rapp/1, identity is the minted tail of a rappid, not the readable owner/slug.
an older rappid whose tail is not 64 lowercase hex characters. It can be read but must not be emitted. Upgrading it requires owner-authorized re-anchoring.
an owner-authorized identity change for exactly one allowed case: provisional upgrade, key rotation, key compromise, or pre-standard key-tag migration.
an owner-signed registry record that revokes a keyed rappid from `revoked_utc` forward.
the one RFC 8785 JCS byte representation of an admissible I-JSON value. See [[Canonicalization]].
the interoperable JSON profile from RFC 7493 that canonicalization is built on.
JSON Canonicalization Scheme, RFC 8785. It fixes member order, escaping, number form and whitespace.
any historical encoding that is not the current canonical form. Live legacy is drift and must be migrated. Sealed re-genesis history is kept as evidence, not as a second dialect.
a SHA-256 digest computed in a named rapp/1 domain. It changes if the content changes. See [[Content Addressing]].
prefixing hash input with an exact space tag and a newline, so the same bytes in different roles get different addresses.
a named domain in which a hash has meaning. rapp/1 stores and looks up by `(space, hash)`, never by a bare 64-hex string.
the closed eleven-field event envelope. It carries a payload particle, a whole-frame wave, chain links and an optional signature. See [[The Frame]].
`H("rapp/1:particle", payload)`, stored as `payload_hash`. It addresses what happened.
`H("rapp/1:wave", frame - {frame_hash, sig})`, stored as `frame_hash`. It addresses the exact unsigned envelope. See [[The Wire]].
an append-only sequence of frames sharing one `stream_id`.
a stream identified directly by a rappid. It chains particles through `prev`; `prev_wave` is null.
a shared `net:*` stream. It chains particles through `prev` and waves through `prev_wave`, and every frame must be signed.
the particle-linked history of a brainstem or stream.
the sequence-zero frame the live chain descends from.
the highest verified frame descending from the registered genesis. Consumers keep heads to detect rollback.
the owner-authorized operation that seals an old chain, publishes a new sequence-zero frame, updates the registry and retires the old bytes under `legacy/`.
a registered `noun.verb` event name.

a `rapp/1-egg` manifest plus, for tree variants, deterministic stored-ZIP contents. It packages a brainstem, rapplication, session, invite, neighborhood, estate, or sealed ciphertext artifact. See [[The Egg]].
the signed, append-only estate root of trust for keys, kinds, genesis records, re-anchors, tombstones, owner succession and canonical-source pointers. See [[The Registry]].
a governed collection of brainstems and neighborhoods sharing one registry and owner succession.
the claim that a key signed an artifact. It needs a valid signature, and does not by itself prove the key was authorized. See [[Trust and Signatures]].
the right of a signer to decide at a given time. It comes from the registry and its owner-succession records.
evidence that bytes or chain links have not changed. Integrity does not imply authorship.
confidence that signed mutable state is recent enough. A valid registry signature proves authenticity, not freshness.
refuse, or report unknown, when evidence is missing, malformed, stale or unverifiable. Never turn "could not check" into a pass.
emits only current canonical values, addresses, identities, frames and egg variants.
validates frames, eggs, signatures, registry state and all refusal conditions before accepting input.
transports or serves artifacts without inventing endpoints or rewriting addressed bytes.

an estate-declared, byte-pinned runtime. Its `grail_id` is `"grail:" || Hb("rapp/1:grail", kernel_bytes)`. Once activated, those bytes are permanent; capabilities grow outside them. See [[The Brainstem Kernel]].
the canonical `rapp-cicd/1-release` payload naming one immutable candidate. See [[RAPP CICD]].
the sequence of release identities that have received user traffic.
an independently observable and isolatable runtime failure domain, governed by `rapp-deploy/1`. See [[RAPP Deploy]].
